record.paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
record.original_question: Does the sequence {ln(k+2)/k!}_{k>=0} form a classical multiplier sequence, meaning that the diagonal operator T on real polynomials defined by T[x^k]=(ln(k+2)/k!) x^k sends every real polynomial with only real zeros to a real polynomial with only real zeros?

evidence.quote: While we believe that the sequence {ln(k + 2)/k!}_0^infinity is a multiplier sequence, we were able to establish such a claim only for an approximating sequence.

Definition 5. A sequence of real numbers {gamma_k}_0^infinity is called a classical multiplier sequence if the associated linear operator T defined by T[x^k]=gamma_k x^k has the property that for every real polynomial p(x), Z_C(T[p(x)])=0 whenever Z_C(p(x))=0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A sequence of real numbers $\{\gamma_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is called a classical multiplier sequence if the linear operator $T$ on $\mathbb{R}[x]$ defined by $T[x^k] = \gamma_k x^k$ has the property that, for every real polynomial $p(x)$ all of whose complex zeros are real, the polynomial $T[p(x)]$ also has only real zeros (the zero polynomial being included by convention).

Determine whether the sequence
$$\gamma_k = \frac{\ln(k+2)}{k!}, \qquad k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots,$$
is a classical multiplier sequence.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that $\{\ln(k+2)/k!\}$ is a classical multiplier sequence appears to remain open: only an approximating sequence has been shown to be a multiplier sequence, and no later resolution of this specific question was located in searches of the literature on multiplier sequences and the Laguerre-Pólya class.

status_evidence.title: On Classical Multiplier Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses classical multiplier sequences and related Csordas–Forgács work, without resolving the ln(k+2)/k! question.
status_evidence.claim: No proof of the ln(k+2)/k! multiplier sequence conjecture is reported in surveys of classical multiplier sequences.

status_evidence.title: Polynomially Interpolated Legendre Multiplier Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on multiplier sequences in the Laguerre-Pólya framework; does not establish that ln(k+2)/k! is a multiplier sequence.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent multiplier-sequence literature does not appear to resolve this specific logarithmic conjecture.
